newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares reach new peak, profit-taking feared.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares reach new peak, profit-taking feared.

text.p: The Danish top-20 KFX share index surged ahead on Friday to end at a new all-time record closing high for the ninth consecutive trading day, with dealers seeing prices holding or slightly falling on Monday.
"Banks and oil and shipping group Moeller dominated. We could see some profit-taking in Moeller on Monday in a becalmed holiday market, sparking possible falls," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index gained an impressive 2.05 point to 185.34 in overall bourse turnover of 1.456 billion crowns. The KFX August future rose 3.30 point to 185.85 with 324 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Leading banks Den Danske, Unidanmark and BG Bank continued their advances amid analyst predictions of more gains over the next half-year.
Den Danske put on eight crowns to 750, Unidanmark, boosted by an SBC Warburg recommendation, went up 14 to 443, while BG Bank finished seven up at 397.
Moeller remained in the limelight with D/S Svendborg and D/S 1912 rising 15,000 and 5,000 crowns respectively to close at 395,000 and 270,000.
Encouraging SAS June passenger traffic increases helped push Copenhagen Airports 25 crowns up to 780.
